How the data becomes sound

  • Ocean: sea temperature → pitch. Warmer water plays a higher note (D minor pentatonic).
  • Ocean: temperature fronts → tremolo. Where water temperature changes sharply (the Gulf Stream, the Southern Ocean front), the note shakes.
  • Ocean: cold polar water (below about 4°C) → glassy pings.
  • Air: sea salt → surf whoosh, dust → sandy hiss and rumble, smoke → fire crackle, sulfate → buzzing industrial drone.
  • Latitude → register or stereo. Register: lower at the equator, higher toward the poles. Stereo: south left, north right.

Data. Ocean: NASA SVS Global Sea Surface Currents and Temperature, ECCO2 model (MIT/JPL), one frame from its March 2007 to March 2008 run. Air: NASA SVS GEOS Aerosols, snapshot of 19 Aug 2025, 20:00 UTC. Values are read back from each frame's colours on a 1° grid: sea temperature via the frame's own 0–32°C colour bar (roughly ±1°C), aerosols as relative colour intensity, not concentrations.
